small_guidance:
- Add `triton.autotune` over `BLOCK_OC ∈ {32,64}`, `BLOCK_SP ∈ {64,128,256}`, `num_warps ∈ {4,8}`, `num_stages ∈ {2,3}` — the current single config (64/128/4w/2s) is almost certainly suboptimal for the (64 OC, 62·62·14 sp, 8·27 K) shape.
- Tile the K loop and use `tl.dot` instead of the outer-product accumulate: load a `[BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K]` weight tile and `[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_SP]` input tile per step (BLOCK_K=8 or 16) so the inner loop becomes tensor-core GEMM rather than 216 sequential rank-1 updates.
- Hoist the kw/kh/kd/ic decomposition out of the hot loop by precomputing strides and looping with nested `for` over (ic, kd, kh, kw) so the index math is constant-folded per iteration.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as an explicit im2col-style GEMM: one program per `(N, OC tile, OHW tile)` with the K dimension = `IC*KD*KH*KW` tiled by BLOCK_K, using `tl.dot` against a `[BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K] x [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_SP]` matmul. This unlocks tensor cores (the current rank-1 accumulate uses only CUDA cores) — the main reason it's 5× slower than cuDNN.
- Switch input/output layout to NDHWC (channels-last) so the GEMM-K axis (IC) is contiguous; the gather for im2col then becomes a coalesced vector load of IC consecutive floats per spatial point.
- Process the full depth dimension inside one program (persistent over OD) so weight tiles stay resident in registers/SMEM across multiple output planes, amortizing weight reloads — weight reuse is the dominant factor for small kernels (27 taps × 8 IC).
